doc.title: Ray Shiner interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 11, 1998

title: Race in New York and friendship with Basie band, Foster and Terry
summary: Black musicians' difficulties; close black friends, the Basie band's tribute after Shorty's death, Clark Terry's kindness.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What was the racial atmosphere during your tenure in New York as far as the studio work, and playing in clubs and that kind of thing?

Black musicians had a hard time, like they still do, except today not so much. But my closest friends were black musicians. The biggest compliment that I’ve ever had was they considered me black. When Shorty, my wife, died, the Basie Band played in town, and Frank Foster is a dear friend of mine, and I know every guy in the band. My first date with Shorty where I took her to hear Basie, she said, “What are you taking me to hear Basie for?” I said, “Well they’ve got to check you out.” © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
You’ve got to get their approval.

Sure. Which was the truth. This is 38 years later, you know, Frank Foster he says, “Where’s Shorty?” I says, “She died last year.” This was in Syracuse. So at intermission he went out and he announced, he said, “We’ll dedicate this concert to Ray Shiner and his wife Shorty.” He says, “Ray, this number is for Shorty.” And they went into “L’il Darlin’” and I cried for twenty minutes. That’s what they thought of me and my wife. They treated me as one of theirs. So I’m very partial, and very blessed. When Clark Terry heard about Shorty, of course he called up when she was sick, and he spoke with her on the phone and I said, “She can’t talk” and she answered him with one word answers on the telephone. And when Clark was here playing at the festival in October, he had the college send a limo to Syracuse to pick me up and bring me here, to sit with his family, to hear the concert, to feed me lunch and to take me back to Syracuse. Clark Terry did that for me, because I’m one of the family, and so is my wife Shorty.
Well I think it’s interesting that the guys that rise to the top are also the nicest guys.

They are. They are. I feel blessed. I feel doubly blessed knowing all the people. At one time I thought of moving to Hamilton I was so happy here. Because everybody at Hamilton has treated me so wonderfully, everybody. I won’t mention names because I’m afraid I’ll miss somebody.
